title: Coordinated trip attenuation and fallback orchestration for dependency/model/tenant circuits
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We need a coordinated circuit-breaker strategy that operates across dependency (external services), model variants, and tenant isolation boundaries. Current per-path breakers are independent and sometimes cause oscillation during region-wide degradation, leading to poor tail latency and unexpected model fallbacks.

Goal: Implement an attenuation layer and orchestration policy that: (1) computes trip thresholds with tenant- and model-aware hysteresis; (2) supports coordinated soft-attenuation (graceful shed percentages) across cohorts/regions; (3) guarantees a safe fallback selection (compatible model variant or cached response) and explicit rollback; (4) surfaces observability for debugging and incident response.

This ticket covers design, simulation, and a canary rollout of the orchestration controller and integration points with the serving runtime and Console routing layer.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can compute per-dependency per-tenant trip scores using latency/error/queue-length signals
Can apply staged attenuation (0.0 -> 0.1 -> 0.5 -> 1.0) to traffic cohorts with configurable hysteresis windows
Fallback selection follows the compatibility matrix and never routes to an incompatible model (no schema/kv mismatch)
Dashboards show trip state, attenuation percentages by region/tenant/model, and predicted vs observed cost delta
Automated integration tests simulate region spike and validate no more than 2x error amplification during steady-state recovery
Canary rolled to 5% of traffic in us-west with safe abort if error rate increases > 15% vs baseline
design_notes:
Key ideas: 1) Trip score = weighted combination of p95 latency exceedance, error rate slope, and queue depth; weights are tenant-profile aware (enterprise tenants have higher sensitivity). 2) Use a finite-state machine for each (tenant, model, dependency) trio with states: OK, WATCH, ATTENUATE, FORCED_OPEN. Transitions require corroboration windows to avoid flapping. 3) Coordinated attenuation: a global controller issues attenuation directives to regional agents; agents locally apply decisions with region-specific thresholds to account for network partitions. 4) Fallback selection: prefer local cache -> cheaper quantized variant -> regional model replica -> hosted fallback API; each fallback option includes a quality budget and a revert timer. 5) Observability: every attenuation action emits an event containing rationale (signals, weights, metric snapshots) and a suggested reversal time.

Trade-offs considered: centralized decisioning simplifies global policies but introduces control-plane coupling; we use a hybrid model where the global controller issues recommended attenuation plans and region agents have a safety-bound to refuse directives if their local health disagrees strongly. This reduces blast radius in split-brain scenarios.
implementation_plan:
1) Extend metrics ingestion pipeline to emit per-tenant p95, error-slope, and queue-metrics with 10s granularity (ENG-INF-203). 2) Implement trip scorer library + FSM in the orchestration service (new microservice: circuit-orch). 3) Region agent adapter to apply attenuation via existing route-weight overrides in the routing table; add a safety check to avoid incompatible fallbacks. 4) Compatibility matrix datastore for model fallbacks (small, strongly-consistent store). 5) Unit + integration tests and chaos scenarios (packet loss, region failover). 6) Canary: staged by tenant cohorts and regions; start 1% -> 5% -> 20%, with automatic abort criteria.

Phases: design (done), prototype (this ticket), integration tests, canary, full rollout.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for trip scorer and FSM (edge cases for oscillation).
- Integration tests that spin up a local region agent and simulate metric bursts to assert attenuation levels.
- Chaos tests: introduce latency spikes in dependent service to ensure attenuations trigger and fallback selection occurs without schema errors.
- Performance test: ensure orchestration directives add <1ms median overhead to routing decision.
- Regression: run against existing circuit-breaker suites to ensure no behavioral regressions for tenants with custom thresholds.
rollout_strategy: Canary with automated aborts. Canary cohorts defined by tenant size and SLA: small dev tenants first, then medium, then enterprise on dedicated capacity. Use feature flag gate for global controller and region-agent compatibility checks. Monitoring alerts will pause rollout on any deviation beyond acceptance criteria. Post-canary we will run a 48-hour soak before increasing traffic share.
monitoring_and_alerting:
Dashboards: trip-state map (by region/tenant/model), attenuation heatmap, fallback counts and latencies, cost impact estimate. Alerts: ATTENUATION_ABORT if error rate increases >15% over baseline for canary cohort; ATTENUATION_LEAK if attenuation directives not honored by agent after 30s; FALLBACK_RATE_SPIKE if fallback rate > baseline*3 for >5min. All attenuation events are logged to an incident timeline stream in Console and emitted to Sentry/Grafana for correlated traces.

Important metrics: p95 latency, error-rate, queue depth, attenuation-% by cohort, fallback-selection success rate, downstream overload counters.

notes_for_oncall: If attenuation directives are observed but no fallback selections are happening and error rates keep growing, abort directives and fall back to pre-defined conservative policy (full open to backup hosted model). Oncall should run the 'attenuation-abort' runbook: https://redwood.runbooks/attenuation-abort and contact SRE lead if rollback fails.
